subject.title: security fix(gateway): defend pre-auth device-signature verify against CPU DoS

question: Should OpenClaw accept this layered pre-auth device-signature DoS hardening as the gateway auth-boundary fix for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/77979?
rationale: The patch appears directionally correct, but it changes unauthenticated gateway auth validation, lockout accounting, and protocol bounds, which needs maintainer/security intent rather than automated cleanup alone.

options.title: Refresh proof and accept
options.body: Ask for current-head terminal or live proof of AUTH_RATE_LIMITED/rate_limited lockout while crypto is skipped, then merge after secops/gateway review and green exact-head checks.

options.title: Request a narrower split
options.body: Keep the schema caps, shape pre-checks, and limiter gate in separate review units if maintainers want smaller security-boundary changes.

options.title: Hold for auth-bounds consolidation
options.body: Pause this PR if maintainers want to coordinate it with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/77538 before landing device-signature hardening.

recommendation.title: Refresh proof and accept
recommendation.body: Ask for current-head terminal or live proof of AUTH_RATE_LIMITED/rate_limited lockout while crypto is skipped, then merge after secops/gateway review and green exact-head checks.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest person-level history for device auth and handshake helper ownership points to steipete, while CODEOWNERS still requires secops review for the security boundary.
